title: Canyon Post
summary: The keeper of the mid-span shrine has ordered books. Books, courier — actual printed pages, thirteen of them, bound, in a shockproof satchel Ila swears is 'mostly shockproof'. The glassroad is slick enough to crack a spine at sixty metres an hour, so carry them like a lullaby: slow hands, clean drifts, no bouncing off the canyon walls no matter how beautifully they sing back.

objectives.label: Take the shockproof satchel from Ila at the old pan
Enter the canyon at the south gate
Deliver the books to the mid-span shrine, spines uncracked

offer.text: A favour in felt and in paper — the shrine-keeper's craving a library, thirteen bound volumes for a shrine that's mostly a shelf and a view. I promised them carried gentle as gossip, and the flats vouched for you, love. They hum your engine kind.
Books. Down the glassroad. In a satchel that is 'mostly' shockproof.

'Mostly' is the honest weather of all containers. The satchel was a choir-horn crate in a former life — it knows how to hold a note and a page both. Carry it smooth, and read none aloud at speed; a story cracks worse than a spine.

accept.text: Slow is a speed too, courier. Drift the bends like bowing a string — the canyon returns what you give it, and you are giving it *literature*.

Ketch here. Fragile books on the glass road. Weight's nought, the risk is all bounce — feather the hop, keep your hover height boring, and if a wall starts singing at you, sing softer. Ila's right about the canyon, worse luck.
The thirteenth book's for you, love, on the keeper's tab. Don't open it mid-run. A good page pulls the eye, and the glassroad is jealous of your eyes.

complete.text: The keeper writes: spines straight, pages dry, one book already being read aloud to the canyon, which has stopped echoing the ends of sentences to argue. You have improved the acoustics of a *gorge*, courier. That's a rare line in any ledger.
Delivered intact. I did look at my book. It's about rivers that used to run here. It's a hopeful little punch in the ribs.
Then it arrived twice — once in the satchel, once in the chest. Payment on the board, love, plus one singing cell, plus the flats' regards, which spend nowhere and matter everywhere.
Nice, quiet hands on that run, kid. The Wren came home without a rattle. Book-learning agrees with you both.
